reviewer: independent AI reviewer (Claude), not a native speaker

issues.explain: เป็น is written 'bpen' here but 'pen' in pairs 5 and 82. The romanisation is inconsistent (the ph/p scheme suggests 'pen').
issues.correction: pen

issues.explain: B repeats A's question word for word and never answers it. A real reply answers first, then asks back.
issues.correction: สบายดีค่ะ แล้วคุณสมชายล่ะคะ — sà-baai-dii khâ, láeo khun sǒm-chaai lâ khá — I'm fine. And you, Somchai?

issues.explain: 'bpen' is inconsistent with 'pen' in the rest of the lesson.
issues.correction: pen

issues.explain: The cue says 'want to buy', so a learner will produce อยากซื้อ. The answer uses อยากได้ ('would like / want to get').
issues.correction: Cue: 'Tell the shop assistant you'd like two pairs of shoes.' or Thai: ผมอยากซื้อรองเท้าสองคู่ครับ — phǒm yàak súe raawng-tháo sǎawng khûu khráp

issues.explain: อยากได้ means 'would like / want (to have)', not literally 'want to buy'.
issues.correction: I'd like two pairs of shoes.

issues.explain: This comes straight after two 'how are you?' greetings that nobody answered. There is no setting (a shop) to explain the line.
issues.correction: Add a framing line that sets the scene in a shop.

issues.explain: Vowel length is inconsistent: รอง has a long ɔɔ, and the lesson writes that as 'aaw' elsewhere, but here it is 'rawng'.
issues.correction: raawng-tháo

issues.explain: 'เสื้อผ้าคู่กัน' and 'how many pairs of matching clothes do you have' is not something people ask. Matching couple shirts are เสื้อคู่, and you would not count them in pairs like this.
issues.correction: รองเท้าคู่นี้ราคาเท่าไหร่คะ — raawng-tháo khûu níi raa-khaa thâo-rài khá — How much is this pair of shoes?

issues.explain: This is an odd, low-frequency question for a beginner.
It does not follow from 'I'd like two pairs of shoes'. A shop context would call for a reply about price or size.
This is the same classifier use as pair 3 (number + คู่), only changed into a กี่คู่ question.
กัน is written 'kan' here but 'gan' in pair 93. The romanisation of ก is inconsistent.
issues.correction: gan

issues.explain: 'ไปหาอะไรกินกันเป็นคู่' ('go eat as a pair/couple') is not idiomatic. Thai would say สองคน or just กัน. The English 'as a couple' is also a forced lead-in for the target word.
issues.correction: เขาสองคนเป็นคู่รักกันใช่ไหมคะ — khǎo sǎawng khon pen khûu-rák gan châi mǎi khá — Those two are a couple, right?

issues.explain: B asks a second unrelated question right after her own pair 4, without waiting for an answer.
It is unclear why she would ask a shoe-buying man out to eat 'as a couple'.
This replies to an invitation to go and eat by proposing to sit here. It does not clearly accept or decline.
ตรง is written 'trong', but ต is written 'dt' elsewhere (dtòk-long, dtâwng). The romanisation is inconsistent.
issues.correction: dtrong-níi

issues.explain: In pair 6 they had not sat down yet. Saying 'I want to sit a little longer' straight after implies they have been sitting for a while. A also speaks twice in a row.
issues.correction: Move it after a line such as 'Shall we go?': ยังครับ ผมอยากนั่งอีกหน่อยครับ

issues.explain: A has just said he wants to stay sitting, and B asks 'will you sit here first?'. That is redundant and does not respond to what he said.
issues.correction: เชิญนั่งก่อนเลยค่ะ — choen nâng gàawn loei khâ — Please, have a seat.

issues.explain: This is the same นั่งตรงนี้ frame as pair 6.
'Will you sit here first?' is vague about what 'first' refers to.
The cue 'He asks what she wants to do' gives no sign of ล่ะ. Learners will say คุณอยากทำอะไรครับ, so the target can only be guessed.
issues.correction: Cue: 'So, what do you want to do then?'

issues.explain: The listed sense is 'what about…?' (X ล่ะ). Here ล่ะ is only an emphatic tag on a question word.
issues.correction: แล้วคุณล่ะครับ — láeo khun lâ khráp — And what about you?

issues.explain: The English drops the 'so / then' nuance of ล่ะ.
issues.correction: So what do you want to do?

issues.explain: It does not answer B's question in pair 8.
ล่ะ is used on a plain statement of desire. It is not a question here, and 'อยากกินข้าวล่ะค่ะ' is not natural Thai. Statement ล่ะ means 'now (I'm off)', as in ไปล่ะ.
issues.correction: ฉันอยากกินข้าวค่ะ แล้วคุณล่ะคะ — chǎn yàak gin khâao khâ, láeo khun lâ khá — I want to eat. What about you?

issues.explain: No native speaker would put ล่ะ here.
The cue 'She says she wants to eat' gives no reason to add ล่ะ.
แล้ว is written lâeo (falling). It is high tone: láeo (ล is low class + mai tho = high).
issues.correction: láeo

issues.explain: B just said what she wants (to eat). Asking 'and what do you want?' ignores her answer.
This is the same frame as pair 9 (คุณอยาก V อะไรล่ะครับ) with ทำ changed to ได้.
It is still not the 'what about X?' use.
issues.correction: แล้วคุณล่ะครับ — láeo khun lâ khráp — What about you?

issues.explain: 'ยังค่ะ' ('not yet') does not answer 'what do you want?'.
The cue does not mention 'Not yet', so the learner cannot produce ยังค่ะ.
issues.correction: Cue: 'Say "not yet" — you probably don't want to go home yet.'

issues.explain: Using คง about your own wishes is possible ('I guess…') but slightly odd, and ค่ะ is doubled.
issues.correction: ฉันคงยังไม่อยากกลับค่ะ

issues.explain: คง (speculation) is clumsy next to a suggestion with นะ. You either propose (เรากินข้าวกันก่อนนะ) or speculate (เราคงจะกินข้าวกันก่อน).
issues.correction: งั้นเราคงต้องกินข้าวกันก่อน — ngán rao khong dtâwng gin khâao gan gàawn — Then we'll probably have to eat first.

issues.explain: The cue says 'you'll' but the answer uses เรา (we), and the cue does not give งั้น.
issues.correction: Cue: 'Then say we'll probably eat first.'

issues.explain: แล้ว is written lâeo (falling). It is high tone: láeo (ล is low class + mai tho = high).
issues.correction: láeo

issues.explain: A has just proposed eating first, and now says he probably has to leave. That contradicts him, and the conversation carries on anyway.
'We'll eat until nighttime' is an odd plan, and it comes right after 'I have to go now'.
This contradicts pair 14 ('I probably have to go now').
The cue says 'you' but the answer uses เรา (we).
issues.correction: กลางคืนที่นี่สวยมากนะครับ — glaang-khuuen thîi-nîi sǔai mâak ná khráp — It's really beautiful here at night.

issues.explain: A answers 'ใช่ครับ' ('yes') to his own previous line.
There is no question from B to confirm.
issues.correction: Give the line to B as a question first, or drop ใช่ครับ.

issues.explain: This is the same ไปเที่ยว + กลางคืน collocation as pair 16.
A has just proposed going out tonight. B's 'tomorrow night?' is a counter-proposal with no signal, such as ไม่ค่ะ or แล้ว.
กลาง is written 'klaang' here but 'glaang' in pairs 15 and 16.
issues.correction: glaang-khuuen

issues.explain: 'ผมทำงานถึงตอนนี้' is unidiomatic. Without มา/จน it does not mean 'I've been working until now'.
issues.correction: พรุ่งนี้ผมทำงานถึงหกโมงเย็นครับ — phrûng-níi phǒm tham-ngaan thǔeng hòk moong yen khráp — Tomorrow I work until six p.m.

issues.explain: 'I work until now' is ungrammatical English and does not describe a real situation.
issues.correction: I've been working until now.

issues.explain: 'He states that he works until the current time' is opaque.
It does not answer B's 'shall we go out tomorrow night?'.
This is the same frame as pair 18 (ผมทำงานถึง + time). Only the time phrase changes.
A speaks twice in a row. This line would answer pair 17 better than pair 18 does.
The cue says 'Ask … okay?', but ตกลงครับ is a statement ('Agreed / OK'). Thai does not make questions with rising intonation. As written, A proposes and then agrees with himself.
issues.correction: เราไปเที่ยวกันนะครับ ตกลงไหมครับ — rao pai-thîiao gan ná khráp, dtòk-long mǎi khráp — Let's go out, OK?

issues.explain: The English 'okay?' does not match the declarative ตกลงครับ.
It ignores B's question 'What do you do for work?'.
This is the same 'proposal + ตกลง(ไหม)?' frame as pair 21.
issues.correction: Use ตกลง for agreeing on a price instead: ตกลงครับ ร้อยบาทนะครับ — dtòk-long khráp, ráawy bàat ná khráp — Deal, 100 baht then.

issues.explain: นะครับ followed by ตกลงไหมครับ is slightly redundant.
They have just agreed to visit a friend's house. 'I have a lot of new clothes' is a non sequitur.
ผมจะใส่ชุดนี้ is more usual. เสื้อผ้าชุดนี้ is acceptable but heavy.
A delivers a long monologue (pairs 23 to 28 are all speaker A).
This is almost identical to pair 24 (only ใหม่ removed). It is a repeat, not a new use.
issues.correction: เสื้อผ้าพวกนี้ซักแล้วหรือยังครับ — sûea-phâa phûak-níi sák láeo rǔe yang khráp — Have these clothes been washed yet?

issues.explain: A repeats his own statement from two lines earlier.
แล้ว is written lâeo (falling). It is high tone: láeo (ล is low class + mai tho = high).
issues.correction: láeo

issues.explain: This continues A's monologue. He is already wearing the shirt, yet just said 'I will wear this outfit'.
The cue says 'these pants', so the learner will produce กางเกงตัวนี้. The Thai omits the noun, and pants have not been mentioned before.
issues.correction: ผมจะใส่กางเกงตัวนี้กับเสื้อครับ — phǒm jà sài kaang-keeng tua níi gàp sûea khráp

issues.explain: ตัวนี้ with no antecedent is unclear. คู่กับเสื้อ would be more natural.
A has just said twice what he will wear, and B asks 'What will you wear?'.
The cue 'What will you wear?' leads to คุณจะใส่อะไรคะ. ชุด is not cued.
Vowel length is inconsistent: ชอบ has a long ɔɔ, and the lesson writes that as 'aaw' elsewhere, but here it is 'châwp'.
issues.correction: chaawp

issues.explain: Asking 'what colour pants do you have?' when he is holding a specific pair is odd.
This mirrors pair 31 (มีกางเกงสี…), as question and answer.
Vowel length is inconsistent: ชอบ has a long ɔɔ, and the lesson writes that as 'aaw' elsewhere, but here it is 'châwp'.
issues.correction: chaawp

issues.explain: Across targets, this repeats the ผมชอบกางเกง… frame from pair 30.
When talking about pants the classifier is ตัว (ตัวนี้สั้น). อันนี้ is colloquial but teaches the wrong classifier.
issues.correction: ตัวนี้สั้นไปครับ — tua níi sân pai khráp — This one is too short.

issues.explain: This is a vague bare statement.
This is the same frame as pair 34, just turned into a question with ไหม.
issues.correction: ผมสั้นดีนะคะ — phǒm sân dii ná khá — Short hair suits you.

issues.explain: A has just said it is short, and B asks 'is it short?'.
แจ็ก is written 'jǎek' (rising). By spelling it is low (jàek), and in practice it is said high (jáek). Rising is wrong either way.
issues.correction: sûea-jáek-gèt

issues.explain: It follows 'Is this one short?' with no link.
ร้อน is written 'rón', which uses the vowel o (as in รถ rót). The vowel is ɔɔ: ráawn.
issues.correction: aa-kàat ráawn

issues.explain: This is the same ถอดเสื้อ(…) frame as pair 36.
issues.correction: ถอดรองเท้าก่อนเข้าบ้านนะครับ — thàawt raawng-tháo gàawn khâo bâan ná khráp — Take your shoes off before entering the house.

issues.explain: Adding เลย would mark the cause better (อากาศร้อน ผมเลยจะถอดเสื้อ).
The cue says 'wash his hands', so the learner will produce ล้างมือ. The Thai omits มือ, and hands have not been mentioned before.
issues.correction: คุณจะไปล้างมือที่ไหนคะ — khun jà pai láang mue thîi-nǎi khá

issues.explain: It has no antecedent: nobody has mentioned dirty hands or washing.
This mirrors pair 39 (จะไปล้างที่…) as question and answer.
After discussing where he will wash (his hands), B asks what he will wash. The order is backwards.
issues.correction: Put it first, or use a different function: ช่วยล้างจานหน่อยได้ไหมคะ — chûai láang jaan nàwi dâi mǎi khá — Could you wash the dishes?

issues.explain: The topic jumps abruptly from washing hands.
B's own question (pair 43, 'which station?') is never answered before she proposes the bus station.
B proposed the bus station, and A now names a third destination (the pier) without reacting.
B asked 'which pier?', and A answers 'shall we go to the pier?'. That does not answer her, and he had already said he is going.
issues.correction: ท่าเรือสาทรครับ — thâa-ruuea sǎa-thaawn khráp — Sathorn Pier.

issues.explain: Across targets, this repeats the เราไป X กันไหม frame from pair 44.
B answers A's question with a question.
A asked whether it is expensive and now asserts it isn't. B's 'how much?' is still not answered with a price.
issues.correction: ค่าโดยสารสิบห้าบาทครับ — khâa-dooi-sǎan sìp-hâa bàat khráp — The fare is 15 baht.

issues.explain: This reuses the แพง predicate from pair 48 (question, then negated statement).
พอดี means 'just right / fits / exactly'. 'พอดีไหมคะ' does not mean 'Is it enough time?'.
issues.correction: จะไปทันไหมคะ — jà pai than mǎi khá — Will we make it in time? / เวลาพอไหมคะ — wee-laa phaaw mǎi khá

issues.explain: The target word พอ only appears inside the compound พอดี, which is a different lexeme.
ตอนไหน for 'when (arrive)' is colloquial. กี่โมง is more natural.
issues.correction: ไปถึงกี่โมงคะ — pai thǔeng gìi moong khá

issues.explain: พอ is long ɔɔ. The system writes long ɔɔ as 'aaw' elsewhere (gàawn, thàawt, sǎawng), so 'phaw' reads as short. The target word's transcription is wrong.
issues.correction: phaaw

issues.explain: This again uses the compound พอดี ('just right'), not พอ ('enough').
issues.correction: เวลาพอครับ — wee-laa phaaw khráp — There's enough time.

issues.explain: 'เวลาพอดี' alone is a little odd. ทันพอดี is more idiomatic.
พอ is long ɔɔ. The system writes long ɔɔ as 'aaw' elsewhere (gàawn, thàawt, sǎawng), so 'phaw' reads as short. The target word's transcription is wrong.
issues.correction: phaaw

issues.explain: A has just said the time is (just) enough, and B asks 'do we have enough time?'.
พอ is long ɔɔ. The system writes long ɔɔ as 'aaw' elsewhere (gàawn, thàawt, sǎawng), so 'phaw' reads as short. The target word's transcription is wrong.
issues.correction: phaaw

issues.explain: 'ไปตรงไป' doubles ไป and is ungrammatical. Directions are ตรงไป or เดินตรงไป. 'แล้วมีร้านกาแฟ' is also clumsy.
issues.correction: ใช่ค่ะ ตรงไปแล้วจะเจอร้านกาแฟค่ะ — châi khâ, trong-pai láeo jà jooe ráan gaa-fae khâ — Yes, go straight and you'll see a coffee shop.

issues.explain: แล้ว is written lâeo (falling). It is high tone: láeo (ล is low class + mai tho = high).
issues.correction: láeo

issues.explain: ร้าน is written 'rán' (short) here but 'ráan' in pair 84.
issues.correction: ráan

issues.explain: 'ใช่ค่ะ' confirms a direction nobody asked about. The previous line was about the fare and time.
The cue is a vague description ('Confirms the direction… mentions a coffee shop is located there') and cannot produce this exact Thai.
issues.correction: Cue: 'Yes — go straight and you'll see a coffee shop.'

issues.explain: แล้ว is written lâeo (falling). It is high tone: láeo (ล is low class + mai tho = high).
issues.correction: láeo

issues.explain: The cue 'they will go straight' does not lead to แล้ว…ก็.
A simply restates B's direction.
When asking about a specific vehicle, คันนี้ไปไหนคะ is more natural.
This mirrors pair 58 (รถสองแถวไป…) as question and answer.
'the station' is vague (which station?), and they wanted the pier.
โกรธ is written krôot (falling). ก is mid class, long vowel, dead syllable, no tone mark = low tone: kròot (gròot). The header entry has the same mistake.
issues.correction: kròot / gròot

issues.explain: 'เขา' (he) has no antecedent and the topic jumps from songthaews.
It is unclear who is angry, why, and where he would go.
โกรธ is written krôot (falling). ก is mid class, long vowel, dead syllable, no tone mark = low tone: kròot (gròot). The header entry has the same mistake.
issues.correction: kròot / gròot

issues.explain: โกรธ is written krôot (falling). ก is mid class, long vowel, dead syllable, no tone mark = low tone: kròot (gròot). The header entry has the same mistake.
issues.correction: kròot / gròot

issues.explain: The direction is wrong: coming to us is มาหาเรา, not ไปหาเรา.
issues.correction: เขามาหาเราไม่ได้ครับ — khǎo maa hǎa rao mâi-dâi khráp — He can't come to see us.

issues.explain: In the cue, 'he' could mean the speaker himself or a third person.
This is the same V + ไม่ได้ (can't) frame as pair 63.
This is the same 'ไป… ไม่ได้' frame as pairs 63 and 64. The 'didn't' sense of ไม่ได้ + V, which the target list names, is never taught.
issues.correction: เมื่อวานฉันไม่ได้ไปค่ะ — mûea-waan chǎn mâi-dâi pai khâ — I didn't go yesterday.

issues.explain: The cue says 'didn't', which suggests ไม่ได้อธิบาย. The answer uses ไม่อธิบาย ('wouldn't explain'). Both are acceptable, but the cue invites the other form.
issues.correction: เขาไม่ได้อธิบายอะไรเลยครับ — khǎo mâi-dâi à-thí-baai à-rai loei khráp

issues.explain: The topic jumps from 'I can't go now' to 'he didn't explain anything', and 'he' is unclear.
'What would he explain?' is a weak follow-up to 'he didn't explain anything'.
issues.correction: ช่วยอธิบายอีกครั้งได้ไหมคะ — chûai à-thí-baai ìik khráng dâi mǎi khá — Could you explain again?

issues.explain: The topic jumps abruptly.
This is the same ทำความสะอาดห้องครัว frame as pair 69, turned into a question.
issues.correction: ห้องครัวอยู่ไหนคะ — hâawng-khruua yùu nǎi khá — Where is the kitchen?

issues.explain: It does not answer 'when will you clean it?'. A is asking permission to look at a kitchen he has just said he will clean.
Vowel length is inconsistent: ขอ has a long ɔɔ, and the lesson writes that as 'aaw' elsewhere, but here it is 'khǎw'.
issues.correction: khǎaw

issues.explain: หลัง is used here as the classifier for houses (บ้านหลังนั้น), not in the taught sense 'after / back'.
issues.correction: หลังกินข้าวเราไปเดินเล่นกันนะครับ — lǎng gin khâao rao pai doen-lên gan ná khráp — After eating, let's go for a walk.

issues.explain: หลัง is the house classifier again, not 'after / back'.
issues.correction: ห้องน้ำอยู่ข้างหลังค่ะ — hâawng-náam yùu khâang-lǎng khâ — The restroom is at the back.

issues.explain: There is no question marker. 'บ้านหลังนั้นของคุณคะ' reads as a statement. It needs เหรอ / ใช่ไหม.
issues.correction: บ้านหลังนั้นเป็นของคุณเหรอคะ

issues.explain: The cue says 'if that house is hers', but B is asking him (ของคุณ = yours). The pronoun is wrong.
issues.correction: Cue: 'She asks if that house is his.'

issues.explain: Vowel length is inconsistent: ของ has a long ɔɔ, and the lesson writes that as 'aaw' elsewhere, but here it is 'khǎwng'.
issues.correction: khǎawng

issues.explain: หลัง is the house classifier again, not 'after / back'.
issues.correction: ผมปวดหลังครับ — phǒm bpùat lǎng khráp — My back hurts.

issues.explain: All three recalls use the same บ้านหลัง นี้/นั้น frame.
Vowel length is inconsistent: ชอบ has a long ɔɔ, and the lesson writes that as 'aaw' elsewhere, but here it is 'châwp'.
issues.correction: chaawp

issues.explain: 'I have two items' is vague and has no context.
issues.correction: เอาอันนี้สองอันครับ — ao an níi sǎawng an khráp — I'll take two of these.

issues.explain: The topic jumps abruptly.
Vowel length is inconsistent: ของ has a long ɔɔ, and the lesson writes that as 'aaw' elsewhere, but here it is 'khǎwng'.
issues.correction: khǎawng

issues.explain: The items are his own ('I have two items'), so 'requesting' the small one with ขอ makes no sense.
issues.correction: Make B the owner/seller.

issues.explain: 'อันเล็กอันนั้น' doubles the classifier. ขออันเล็กครับ is more natural.
issues.correction: ขออันเล็กครับ — khǎaw an lék khráp

issues.explain: The cue does not mention 'that' (อันนั้น).
Vowel length is inconsistent: ขอ has a long ɔɔ, and the lesson writes that as 'aaw' elsewhere, but here it is 'khǎw'.
issues.correction: khǎaw

issues.explain: ชาย has a long vowel. Here it is written 'chai' (short), while the same lesson writes สมชาย as sǒm-chaai. This is the target word's own transcription.
issues.correction: phûu-chaai

issues.explain: There is no question marker, so 'ผู้ชายคนนั้นของคุณคะ' reads as a statement.

summary: The Thai is mostly grammatical at sentence level, but the lesson has three systematic weaknesses. (1) Phonetics: two high-frequency words have the wrong tone throughout. แล้ว is written lâeo instead of láeo (pairs 11, 14, 27, 54, 55), and โกรธ is written krôot instead of kròot, including in the header. There are also a vowel-quality error (ร้อน 'rón' in 38) and a tone error (แจ็ก 'jǎek' in 36). Long ɔɔ/aa is often written short (พอ 'phaw', ชาย 'chai', ของ/ขอ/ชอบ), and the romanisation switches between bp/p, dt/t and g/k. Pair 7's หน่อย 'nàwi' is correct. (2) Sense drift: หลัง is taught three times as the house classifier instead of 'after / back' (72–74). พอ is replaced by the compound พอดี (51–52). ล่ะ is never taught in its 'what about X?' function and is forced onto a statement in pair 10. ไม่ได้ never covers 'didn't', and ทิ้ง never covers 'leave behind'. (3) Weak distinctness and coherence: recalls often reuse one frame with a single word swapped (ผู้ชาย/ผู้หญิงคนนั้น, บ้านหลัง…, ทำงานถึง…, เสื้อผ้า 24/26). Many lines were generated per target and only then chained together. Speakers answer their own lines (16, 21), ask questions that were just answered (29, 35, 53), contradict themselves (14→15), or refer to things never mentioned (39 hands, 28 pants, 60 'he'). Cues sometimes cannot produce the Thai: 'buy' vs อยากได้, the missing 'not yet', ล่ะ that is never cued, and 'hers' vs ของคุณ. Specific grammar or naturalness defects include ไปตรงไป (54), ตกลงครับ used as a question (21), ไปหาเรา for 'come see us' (63), missing question markers (73, 79), and 'ทำงานถึงตอนนี้' (18). The likely causes are per-word sentence generation with no dialogue-level planning, a sense check that accepts any occurrence of the word's string, and romanisation that is not checked against Thai tone rules.
